newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 15.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
GOVERNMENT ASKS DGCA FOR REPORT

The government asked the Director General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) to submit a report on the delay in installing the Raytheon secondary surveillance radars and navigational aids at the Delhi and Bombay airports. These were scheduled to be in place by October 1995. The government asked the DGCA to identify the causes of the delay and submit its report within one week. Meanwhile, the officials continued to deliberate on the causes of the mid-air collision near Delhi, but pointed out that the final answers would come only after completion of the inquiry by Delhi High Court judge R. Lahoti.
The Economic Times
FOUR CONSORTIA SAY NO TO FINANCIAL CLOSURE

Giving a severe setback to the privatisation of basic telecommunication services, four consortia that have been granted letters of intent refused to go in for financial closure. Tata-Bell Canada, Hughes Ispat, Essar-Bell Atlantic and RPG-NTT pointed to several post-tender conditions imposed by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) that threatened financial viability of these projects, thus making financial closure impossible. A fifth, HFCL-Bezeq Telecom, was already in court contesting DoT's handling of the process.
VIDEOCON BAGS 45 BILLION RUPEE NAPHTHA CRACKER PROJECT

Videocon International outbid the Hindujas to bag the 45 billion rupee naphtha cracker project at Mangalore in Karnataka. The state government cleared the deal with several riders concerning the environmental impact of the project. The site for the project is yet to be decided. The project will start once the ecological impact study is completed. Karnataka State Industrial Investment Development Corporation is to pick up 11 percent stake in the project. Videocon has tied up with Samsung of South Korea for the downstream project.
PFIZER'S HOPES OF SETTING UP ARM REVIVES

The Industry Ministry has asked U.S drug multinational Pfizer Inc to make a fresh presentation of their proposal for setting up a fully owned subsidiary. The latest development comes after almost one year of reluctauce on the part of the Foreign Investment Promotion Board and the Industry Ministry to clear the proposal. The $8.3 billion drug firm is likely to approach the ministry after January next year.
MANMOHAN FOR REDEFINING STATE'S ROLE AS REGULATOR

India must complete its unfinished agenda of economic reforms, said former finance minister Manmohan Singh. He said there was a consensus on reforms and called for urgent attention to issues like higher saving and investment, decentralisation, modernisation of agriculture, creation of social safety nets and mobilisation of resources of the civil society. He said fiscal imbalances must be corrected to boost rate investment, lower inflation, improve the balance of payments position and reduce real interest rates. He also called for taking a fresh look at the state's role as a producer and a regulator.
TWENTY BLN RUPEE GILT AUCTION ANNOUNCED

The government has announced an auction of 20 billion rupee, five-year paper. The auction is scheduled for November 26. This is the first tranche of government securities to be issued following the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) announcement of the monetary policy for the second half of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) on October 19, 1996. RBI sources said this paper would be eligible for ready forward purchases.
Financial Express
BPL CELLULAR FILES FOR NASDAQ

BPL Cellular Holdings is getting its American Depositary Receipts (ADR) listed on the Nasdaq. BPL seeks to raise about $200 million through an initial public offering of 12.5 million ADRs with a greenshoe option to increase the issue by 15 percent. Morgan Stanley is managing the deal. BPL Cellular, which started operations in October 1995, reported operating revenue of $7.7 million for the year ended March 31, 1996, and a net loss of $117 million. Analysts are viewing the BPL move with caution in view of the former's shaky financial performance and political uncertainty in India.
PROACTIVE ROLE SOUGHT FOR FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS

The role of financial institutions (FIs) in the management of companies was criticised by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII). A draft corporate governance code, drawn up by CII, stressed on greater involvement of FI directors on a company's board to ensure a more transparent management and for protecting small shareholders. The paper pointed out that FIs supported the existing management on the grounds of stability. The CII draft assumes significance in light of the alleged involvement of top ITC executives in the foreign exchange regulations case.
Business Standard
OFFICIALS DISCUSS QUANTUM OF PETROLEUM PRICE HIKE

The move to raise prices of petroleum products gained momentum with the cabinet secretariat convening a meeting of officials of the petroleum and finance ministries to discuss the issue. The cabinet secretariat meeting debated on the quantum of price hike of each product that could keep the oil economy on an even keel. Informed sources confirmed a hike in the prices of petroleum products was inevitable and could come any time after the winter session of parliament.
ESSAR TO DIVEST 30 PCT IN REFINERY

Essar group plans to rope in a foreign partner who will pick up a 25 to 30 percent stake in its 53 billion rupee refinery project. As part of the divestment strategy, the group also plans to offload a 40 percent stake in a new company which has been floated by spinning off the pelletisation plant under Essar Steel. The choice was narrowed down to the Japanese trading giant Mitsui and the South Korean conglomerate Hanbo after negotiations with prospective buyers.
